title: AI used to reply. Now it acts first. Claude Duet is the start.
subtitle: Claude Duet checks your apps, briefs you each morning and drafts the work before you ask, then waits for your yes. If you already live in Claude, here is what changes, and what it costs.

From asking to approving: today you open Claude, copy the email thread, the invite and your notes, paste them in and ask; with Claude Duet a morning brief, meeting prep, a draft reply and a note to the team arrive first, each waiting for your yes.

status: Fact check on these words (1 November 2026): every other line passed or was already signed off by Krish. 5 lines need his sign-off in his own words before publishing: "Anthropic opened it on 21 October as a research preview (an early, unfinished release) for people on Claude's paid Pro and Max plans in the US (off a waitlist, for now)." | "Every few hours it checks the apps you have connected: Gmail, Slack, your calendar, HubSpot, or any of the "over 6,000 connectors and plugins" (the links that let Claude reach other apps) that Anthropic counts." | "Vo, who hosts the podcast "How I AI", put Duet to work on an inbox and a sales pipeline, and found that after the first few tasks, nothing "would pull me back in"." | "The reviewer at Every found two more gaps." | "Duet is an early example of AI that starts the work itself and brings it to you for a decision."
Both videos are finished and passed an independent review; watch them at full size before you press Approve for publish.
